label: Stop 4: The Oude Kerk, the Old Church

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. We're in a small square, with a big church in the middle.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It's surrounded by buildings. It feels almost hidden.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the Oude Kerk. It means the Old Church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's the oldest building in Amsterdam still standing, by most accounts, though we'll say "by most accounts."

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why am I not surprised?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A wooden chapel stood here by about 1213.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The stone church was consecrated in 1306, to Saint Nicholas.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Patron saint of sailors.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Right. Fits a harbor town.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And now the surroundings. It's busy tonight.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. The church stands in the old quarter called De Wallen.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This is the red light district.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There are windows behind the church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Please be respectful, and do not photograph the workers.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Understood. They're working.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. And a small statue near the church, called Belle, carries a message of support for sex workers.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Now the spooky part.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Here's the thing. This one doesn't need a legend.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The record is spooky enough.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Go on.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The floor of the church is made of gravestones.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: About 2,500 of them. Under them, roughly 60,000 Amsterdam citizens were buried.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Burials inside the church continued until 1865.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Sixty thousand.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Under the floor. You walk on them.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's more than a lot of towns.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. And it's all documented.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, I'm properly spooked. And no ghost needed.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Stamp it. Record.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Record. Now the famous names. Rembrandt's wife Saskia van Uylenburgh was buried here in 1642.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the composer and organist Jan Pieterszoon Sweelinck is buried here too.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He lived from 1562 to 1621.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Saskia. Oh.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There's a lovely detail. On one morning in March, the sun briefly lights her tomb.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: 9 March, at about 8:39 in the morning.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's beautiful. Record?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's what the church's own information says.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll call it record, with the caution that we can't check the sunlight ourselves.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fine. What happened in the 16th century?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1566, the Beeldenstorm. It means the Statue Storm.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Protestant crowds destroyed religious images across the Low Countries.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Here, most of the church's art and fittings were destroyed.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: An altarpiece by Jan van Scorel was lost.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Only the ceiling paintings survived.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1578 the city switched sides and the church became Protestant, Calvinist.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It still is. It has four organs, and one of them, built in 1724 by Christian Vater, is considered among the finest Baroque organs in Europe.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wait, how does this connect to the miracle?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Good question. Each March, Catholics in Amsterdam walk a silent procession called the Stille Omgang, in memory of a miracle said to have happened in 1345.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a tradition, and we'll hear more of it at the next stop.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Tally. Ghost stories, nought.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Real history, three.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: But this one's the spookiest.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: By far. Sixty thousand people, under your shoes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Is it open now?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Probably not, this late. It does host art exhibitions today, and it's an active church.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Check the hours another day.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. This is the champagne moment, isn't it?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. You're in a lively quarter.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There are bars and cafes near here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Take a half hour. Sit down. Warm up.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Raise a glass to the sixty thousand?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A quiet toast would be fine.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A very quiet toast. Pause the tour, everyone.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: We'll wait.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: When you're ready, the next stop is the Begijnhof.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's in the middle of the old center, near a square called the Spui.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: From here you go south through the center, toward the Spui.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A narrow passage off the pedestrian street, the Kalverstraat, leads into the courtyard.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Pedestrian street, narrow passage.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Hidden door.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Hidden is the word. And please keep your voice down once you're in.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: People live there.
